Marta L: We just got a chargeback notice from Helix Labs for INV-HEL-2026-221 ($3,250). Stripe dispute id dp_1Zx9C. Reason: 'unauthorized'. Deadline in 7 days. @Priya can you own?
Priya (Payments): On it. Need billing_project, card last4, and the billed window to pull logs.
Marta L: billing_project=helix-prod, card last4=3321, billing email billing@helix.example, window 2026-10-04..2026-10-10.
Alex H: Quick ask: pull request logs for that window with request_id, api_key_id, tokens, ip_address, response_code. Prefer CSV. Also get key creation event.
Jordan (CS): CS reached out to customer; they say they didn't authorize the traffic and want a refund. I've placed account on billing-review and disabled write keys. Notified customer.
Stripe-Bot: dispute.created id=dp_1Zx9C amount=3250 currency=USD reason=unauthorized created=1740000000
Priya (Payments): From a quick look: 630k tokens concentrated on 2026-10-06 from api_key key_hlx77; IPs 3.210.14.99 (us-east) and 185.62.9.10 (vpn). Key created by "emma.helix@helix.example" on 2026-09-28 via console. No password reset around key creation.
Alex H: Add geo lookups and user-agent counts. If calls came from a VPN IP after legit creation, we can argue possible compromise and show hold + keys disabled.
Priya (Payments): I'll assemble: invoice PDF, usage CSV, key lifecycle, support thread, IP geos, hold action. Will submit to Stripe and paste submission id here.
Marta L: Thanks. Keep artifacts in ticket FT-6110. If customer insists on provisional refund, route to me.
